## 17. CARD MODE ADDENDUM

output_mode is card_mode: the text fills a short card for a GeoAI Researcher / Model Analyst,
shown with four stat tiles and two Hull-wide dashboard panels (01: signed Geo-SMILE coefficient
against the exact single-LSOA W1 shift for all 168 LSOAs, coloured by LISA class; 02: LISA map
of signed GeoSensitivity). The card is CITY-WIDE: report the main Hull-wide results of both
branches and the explanation-quality evaluation. Do not build the narrative around a single
LSOA; an extreme value may appear only as a property of the distribution. This section replaces
section 14 "Length and form" and its bolding rule. Every other section, including prohibited
claims and the self-check, still applies.

Technical language is expected: exact values, test statistics, correlation values, sign
conventions and LISA classes are allowed. Keep the sign convention exact: the signed coefficient
is a relative contribution to the coalition W1, not a direction of crime change. ATT
Faithfulness (across-model r between predictive R2 and ATT accuracy) and intervention impact
(top 20 against random masking) are different measures: never conclude one from the other.

No repetition: every figure appears ONCE on the card. The panels already print the figures in
researcher_diagnostics.shown_on_panels, so neither tiles nor sections cite them; refer to the
panel instead ("panel 01"). A tile figure is not cited again in the sections, not even its
first number.

Return ONLY one JSON object with exactly these keys:

- "headline": one sentence, at most 20 words.
- "tiles": exactly 4 objects {"value": ..., "label": ...}. value is one figure from the
  evidence (at most 8 characters); label is at most 8 words naming the quantity exactly
  (e.g. "Geo surrogate held-out R2"). Choose explanation-quality figures.
- "section_01": at most 75 words, how the explanation behaves across Hull (panels 01-02): the
  signed against absolute ranking result and what the sign means, how skewed the single-LSOA
  shift distribution is, how much of LISA is significant, and the Feature branch (leading
  global features, crime-history share, location players' global ranks).
- "section_02": at most 75 words, explanation quality: whichever of fidelity (both branches),
  expert-region accuracy, intervention impact, neighbour stability, seed consistency (both
  branches) and ATT Faithfulness (both branches) the tiles do not already give, with the
  limitation that matters most.
- "footer": one limitation, at most 15 words.

Key-term counts: 1-2 in the headline and 2-4 in EACH section. Tiles and footer carry no
markup.

Highlighting markup (you choose what to mark):

- wrap every figure you cite as [[n:...]], e.g. [[n:14%]];
- wrap the key terms a planner should catch when scanning as [[t:...]]. This is required,
  not optional: keep to the counts given above, each at most 4 words (the finding phrase
  itself, the leading feature names, or the key place names). Before answering, count the
  [[t:...]] spans and fix any count outside the range;
- no other markup and no markdown bold.

Every figure must be copied or rounded from EVIDENCE_JSON (shares as percentages:
0.139 -> 14%). Do not compute new figures and do not cite a figure that is not supplied.

ILLUSTRATIVE_NARRATIVE in the user message shows the expected structure, order, tone and
markup density. It is an example of wording, not evidence: take every figure from
EVIDENCE_JSON, and write your own sentences.

illustrative_narrative.headline: Geo-SMILE's [[t:signed ranking]] tracks exact masking and is stable, but [[t:ATT Faithfulness]] is not established.
illustrative_narrative.section_01: The [[t:signed coefficient]] tracks the exact shift (panel 01); its absolute value does not ([[n:-0.29]]), so the sign marks a relative contribution to the coalition W1. Shifts are skewed: median [[n:6.4]], 90th percentile [[n:22.0]], maximum [[n:176.7]]. Most LSOAs are [[t:not significant]] in LISA (panel 02). In the Feature branch, [[t:crime history]] carries [[n:61%]]; location players rank only [[n:20]] and [[n:23]] of [[n:32]].
illustrative_narrative.section_02: Feature surrogate fidelity is [[n:0.983]]. Masking the top 20 shifts predictions [[n:26.22]] more than random sets, an [[t:intervention impact]], not faithfulness. Feature ranks are less reproducible across seeds ([[n:0.69]]). Across [[n:10]] models, predictive R2 and ATT accuracy are weakly related ([[n:0.15]] Geo, [[n:-0.12]] Feature), so [[t:ATT Faithfulness]] is not established.
illustrative_narrative.footer: Attributions are associational; local LISA p-values are unadjusted.

global_geo.note: GeoSensitivity is the Geo-branch area-data SMILE coefficient: masking an LSOA replaces all of its model inputs with Hull training medians, and the coefficient attributes the resulting prediction shift to that LSOA. It is not latitude or longitude feature attribution.

global_spatial_pattern.note: LISA classes describe clustering of signed GeoSensitivity (area-data design). They are not crime hotspots and not latitude/longitude effects.

content.headline: Geo-SMILE's [[t:signed coefficient ranking]] is reproducible and spatially clustered, but [[t:ATT Faithfulness]] is weak.
content.section_01: The [[t:signed Geo-SMILE coefficient]] closely tracks the exact single-LSOA W1 shift (panel 01, [[n:0.982]]), but absolute values do not (Spearman [[n:-0.29]]). The distribution is right-skewed: median [[n:6.4]], 90th percentile [[n:22.0]], max [[n:176.7]]. LISA detects [[n:9]] high-high and [[n:9]] low-low clusters, but most LSOAs ([[n:142]]) are [[t:not significant]] (panel 02). In the Feature branch, [[t:crime history]] dominates (61%), with latitude and longitude ranked only 23rd and 20th.
content.section_02: Geo surrogate fidelity is [[n:0.948]]. Top-20 Geo masking shifts predictions [[n:26.22]] more than random, an [[t:intervention impact]], not faithfulness. Geo explanations are highly reproducible: ATT stability Jaccard [[n:1.0]], seed rank Spearman [[n:0.963]]. Across 10 models, ATT Faithfulness is weak (Geo [[n:0.15]], Feature [[n:-0.12]]). Local LISA p-values are unadjusted.
